newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO HAVE MATURED ON THE EUROPEAN STAGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO HAVE MATURED ON THE EUROPEAN STAGE.

text.p: Monaco have come a long way since their first taste of European club soccer 34 years ago.

"It was in the 1963-64 season. We had won both the French league and the Cup the season before and we were playing the European Cup for the first time," the club's general manager Henri Biancheri recalled of their tie against Internazionale.
Inter won 1-0 in Milan before taking the second leg 3-1 in Marseille.
"We had to play the second leg in Marseille because the Louis II stadium was too small at the time," said Biancheri.

Monaco returned to the San Siro stadium last week with a different attitude, although the result in the first leg of their UEFA Cup tie belied the change as the competition favourites crashed to a surprise 3-1 defeat.
The away goal, however, gives them hope that they can turn the tie around in Tuesday's home leg and reach their second European final.
Since 1963, the team from the principality have won three more league titles and are at present heading towards a fourth, the sixth in their history.
Their status in Europe has also improved dramatically.
Thanks to coach Arsene Wenger, hired from Nancy in 1987, Monaco played in the Cup Winners' Cup final in 1992 and two semifinals -- the 1994 European Cup and the 1990 Cup Winners' Cup.
The likes of Glenn Hoddle, George Weah and Juergen Klinsmann have enjoyed the Monte Carlo sunshine for a while before pursuing brilliant careers elsewhere.
The 1963 Inter clash may have been the starting point of the whole story. Seeing their team play against such stars as Sandro Mazzola, Giacinto Facchetti and Brazil's Jair gave Prince Rainier ideas.
"The palace decided they wanted a big European team and it allowed us to grow as years went by. We got the men and we got the means," said Biancheri.
"A first step was taken when Arsene Wenger joined. Now Monaco have gone one step further and we're not afraid to tackle teams like Internazionale, who were like the Himalayas for us back in 1963."
At the time, he said, Monaco's players were just happy to take part in European competition. Now they start matches wanting to win.
"The frame of mind has changed and that's why French players have become so attractive for foreign clubs," he said.
Monaco should know. They have seen the likes of Youri Djorkaeff and Lilian Thuram leave for Italy while Thierry Henry is among the most coveted players in Europe.
Since 1963, Monaco have built a new Louis II stadium on the seafront and a training centre, run by former player Claude Puel.
"Wenger brought professionalism to Monaco and then we struggled to replace him. But now with Jean Tigana, we are back on the right track," Puel said.
"Now the only thing missing is a major European title."
